result.summary: Resolves Include-What-You-Use (IWYU) warnings across fuzz tests, fuzz utilities in `src/test/fuzz`, and several internal headers and modules in `src/`. Configures CI to treat IWYU warnings in these files as errors, reformatting the CI list of enforced files to one file per line. Also adds a mapping for standard C library cookie I/O symbols in the IWYU mappings file.
result.problem: Fuzz targets and several core headers rely on transitive includes and contain unused headers. Without explicit includes, CI cannot enforce IWYU compliance on the fuzz suite to prevent future header bloat and unintended dependencies.
evidence: PR description links to developer notes and notes that 'This PR continues the ongoing effort to enforce IWYU warnings.'
result.scope_notes: Very large mechanical diff spanning nearly 190 files, primarily consisting of added, removed, or rearranged `#include` directives and forward declarations.
result.changed_since_previous: Removed superseded dependencies on #36805 and #36807, rebasing exclusively on #36844.
result.card: Fixes Include-What-You-Use (IWYU) warnings across fuzz tests in src/test/fuzz and select source headers, enabling strict CI error enforcement for them. It adjusts headers and forward declarations across nearly 190 files to eliminate reliance on transitive includes. This continues ongoing internal maintenance to automate include hygiene across the codebase. The PR is a draft based on #36844.

risk.why: Mistakes would lead to compilation failures across unsupported compiler configurations rather than runtime faults or consensus issues.
